articleSummary: Guangxi’s Nanning reports earlier mosquito activity due to rapid spring warming, led by Aedes albopictus (the white-striped/Asian tiger mosquito), a principal dengue and chikungunya vector. Seek medical care promptly if fever, rash, or joint pain develop. As temperatures rise, ticks are also becoming active. Outdoors, thoroughly check for ticks on return home, focusing on the scalp, neck, and body. Ticks are small but swell after feeding; remove them slowly and vertically to prevent rupture, and avoid twisting or pulling forcefully. Tick saliva can numb bites, making detection harder. Before outdoor activities, use DEET-based repellents; if fever, fatigue, headache, nausea, or vomiting occur after exposure, seek medical care and report the exposure history.

articleSummary: Lassa fever is an acute viral haemorrhagic illness caused by Lassa virus (Arenaviridae), first identified in 1969 in Lassa, Nigeria. articleSummary: World Malaria Day 2026 falls on April 25 to raise awareness of malaria, a mosquito-borne disease caused by Plasmodium parasites. WHO notes that a significant proportion of malaria deaths occur among children under five, who are more susceptible because their immune systems are immature and lack prior exposure, unlike adults in endemic areas who develop partial immunity. Complications in children include severe anaemia and cerebral malaria; deterioration can be rapid if diagnosis is late. Dr. Rajesh Kumar of Paras Health, Gurugram, emphasizes that under-fives’ limited physiological reserves, combined with environmental risks like poor housing, stagnant water, and inconsistent net use, worsen outcomes. Adults show classic fever and chills, while children may present crying, poor feeding, vomiting, seizures, breathing problems, or unconsciousness. Prevention: insecticide-treated nets, repellents, and eliminating standing water; early recognition and prompt treatment are crucial.

articleSummary: In Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil, UFMS researchers have developed a rapid diagnostic method using infrared spectroscopy combined with artificial intelligence to detect dengue, chikungunya, and yellow fever from a single sample in about one minute. The assay achieves up to 95% accuracy, differentiating infected from non-infected individuals and distinguishing diseases with similar symptoms, validated against conventional PCR. It analyzes the sample’s molecular signature rather than targeting a specific pathogen, enabling faster, cheaper testing with minimal reagents and preparation. Equipment costs around R$10,000 with an expected 10,000 hours of use; each analysis takes roughly one minute. Samples come from Lacen-MS and Evandro Chagas (PA); the approach is being tested within a broader effort for seven neglected diseases (including tuberculosis, leishmaniasis, malaria, and Chagas) via a single predictive model. An ongoing outbreak in the Dourados region underscores clinical and public health relevance; saliva-based testing is also being explored for later expansion.

articleSummary: China bans immediately all poultry and derived products imports from Chile to block avian influenza outbreaks detected in Chile and safeguard its livestock biosecurity. The ban disrupts Chilean poultry trade; China accounted for about 15% of Chile’s poultry exports in 2022, roughly 29,000 tonnes, and was the third-largest market. In Chile, authorities report avian influenza outbreaks across several regions and urge backyard poultry owners to reinforce biosecurity, avoiding contact with wild birds. Suspected cases should be reported to SAG. Bird signs include loss of appetite, uncoordinated movement, ruffled plumage, respiratory discharge, diarrhea, soft eggs, swelling, blue-tinged wattles/crests, prostration, or death. Early detection is stressed to contain spread during migratory periods.

articleHeadline: Pesquisadores poloneses identificam parasita Cryptosporidium em latrinas romanas
articleSummary: Polish researchers analyzed mineralized waste from Roman latrines in the Lower Mesia Inferior province (northern Bulgaria), identifying Cryptosporidium alongside Taenia eggs and Entamoeba histolytica. Material from Novae near Svishtov indicated a high parasite burden, while Marcianópolis (Devnya) yielded no parasites. The team rehydrated crusts, examined them at 400x, and confirmed results with ancient DNA analysis and ELISA. Study underscores paleoparasitology’s role in reconstructing historical disease burdens and informing modern public health perspectives.

articleSummary: Yellow fever in São Paulo state: Three new cases were reported on April 23, 2026, by the state Health Secretariat. Two deaths occurred in residents of the Vale do Paraíba (Lagoinha)—a 56-year-old man and a 53-year-old man. A third case from the Sorocaba region (Araçariguama) involved a 43-year-old man who recovered. The previous week saw three more cases, including a 38-year-old man from Cunha who died; two Cruzeiro residents recovered. All cases this year had no vaccination history. The State Health Secretariat reiterates that the yellow fever vaccine, which is free, is the most important and effective prevention. Transmission is mainly via mosquitoes Haemagogus and Aedes aegypti. The reports underscore ongoing circulation of yellow fever in the Vale do Paraíba region and surrounding areas, highlighting vaccination and mosquito-control measures.

articleHeadline: Florida And Nevada Lawmakers Move To Block Monkey Imports Over Biosecurity Fears - Tampa Free Press
articleSummary: U.S. lawmakers introduced the PRIMATE Act to ban importation of nonhuman primates for laboratory research, exempting accredited zoos, and to shut the U.S. supply chain for labs. Sponsored by Florida Republican Greg Steube and Nevada Democrat Dina Titus, the bill would amend the Tariff Act of 1930. It authorizes Customs and Border Protection to seize illegal shipments and imposes up to $50,000 per primate in fines. From 2021 to 2024, nearly 100,000 monkeys were brought into the United States for laboratory work. The sponsors cite biosecurity risks and disease threats, naming tuberculosis, Salmonella, and herpes B virus, and point to supply chains in China. Local incidents bolster concerns: in Immokalee, Florida, monkeys overheated and died at a facility; in Miami, a monkey was sent to a medical waste facility. Support from PETA, Emory researchers, and Neal Barnard is noted; Treasury Secretary would finalize regulations within one year if enacted.
notes: 記事は米国（対象国外）での政策動向であり、中国のサプライチェーンに言及されているが、中国での感染症イベント発生は報告されていない。フロリダのサル施設での個別インシデント（過熱死）は孤立事例であり、流行性疾患アウトブレイクではない。本件は予防的立法の追跡として適切だが、シグナルトリアージの対象とはならない。

articleSummary: Recife, Brazil, launches Day D of Arboviruses Response in Schools to intensify prevention of Aedes aegypti and combat dengue, Zika, and chikungunya across 18 municipal schools in eight health districts, with the opening at 8:00 at Escola Municipal de Água Fria. The event on Friday, April 24, 2026, mobilizes 223 health professionals from the Recife Health Department (Sesau) and aims to reach about 26,400 residents. Morning activities (8:00–12:00) will feature educational games, exhibits, and messages to eliminate mosquito breeding sites. Surrounding the schools, Surveillance and Primary Care teams will conduct mutirões, visiting roughly 6,000 properties for home inspections, larviciding, water-tank screening, and removal of breeding habitats. In high-risk areas, waste collection is conducted with the Emlurb partnership to reduce litter that supports vector proliferation. Citizens can report suspected foci via SUS Ombudsman (0800 281 1520), Conecta Recife, or the city website.

articleSummary: Hand, Foot and Mouth Disease (HFMD) outbreak in Vietnam at the Pediatrics Department of 108 Military Central Hospital highlights rapid EV71-associated complications. HFMD is caused by Coxsackievirus A16 and Enterovirus 71; EV71 can cause encephalitis, meningitis, myocarditis, and pulmonary edema. The disease progresses in phases: incubation 3–7 days; prodrome 1–2 days with fever, sore throat, poor appetite; acute phase 3–10 days with oral ulcers, drooling, and vesicular rash on hands, feet, knees, buttocks. A four-tier severity scale guides care: 2A–2B signals potential circulatory/neurological risk; 3 indicates severe neuro-cardiopulmonary involvement; 4 shock or respiratory failure. A 12-month-old girl (N.M.C.) presented with fever 39.3°C, HR 152, RR 32, vesicular rash; diagnosed HFMD grade 2A; monitored continuously; stable, with isolation to prevent cross-infection. Home care emphasizes hygiene, hydration, gentle fever control, and urgent medical evaluation for red flags.

The message: malaria elimination is a starting point for ongoing control, not the end.

articleHeadline: Casos e mortes por meningite deixam municípios de MT em alerta  | Diario de Cuiabá
articleSummary: Meningitis cases in Mato Grosso trigger municipal alerts. Through epidemiological week 14 (Mar 29–Apr 4), the state reports 24 confirmed cases and 13 under investigation. Cuiabá accounts for seven cases from January to Apr 21, including two deaths; the city will offer meningitis vaccination on Saturday, Apr 25, during the Dia D influenza vaccination drive, though vaccines are available year-round at all 72 Family Health Units (USFs). In Sinop, about 503 km north, a 5-year-old girl and a teenage girl from the same family died this week. The 5-year-old contracted meningitis type B, for which there is no SUS vaccine; private doses cost roughly R$700–R$800. Sinop SMS says cases are monitored with no outbreak risk, with active contact tracing, sanitary measures, school cleaning, and temporary suspension of classes at Escola Municipal Tempo de Infância. Meningitis is inflammation of the meninges and can be viral or bacterial; vaccines include meningococcal C (MenC) and ACWY under SUS schedules.
